money_at_stake.rationale: TSMC's own 2026-07-16 announcement commits a further $100B to at least four more 2nm-or-more-advanced Arizona fabs, on top of the $165B already pledged, taking total planned Arizona/US investment to $265B across up to 10 fabs and two advanced-packaging plants. $265B is more than double the GT_100B floor of $100B, so this is not a boundary call. The candidate's own occurrence record independently states the same $265B/10-fab/two-packaging-facility figures, and this run's own fetch of a secondary but independently reachable article confirms the same numbers, so the figure is corroborated across two sources.

evidence.claim: TSMC's additional Arizona investment adds to the $165 billion already pledged for Arizona, taking the chipmaker's total planned US spending to $265 billion, and the expansion could eventually give the Arizona campus 10 fabs and two packaging plants, funding at least four additional fabs producing chips at the 2nm node and below.

public_reach.rationale: As close to a pure-play clean read as this stage produces. TSMC is not a supplier behind the money, it IS the money: the $265B is TSMC's own committed capital expenditure, spent and disclosed by a single listed issuer (NYSE: TSM / TWSE: 2330), with no state, private, or sanctioned intermediary in the chain at all. Held just short of the 85+ pure-play ceiling's top rather than at 100 only because the underlying leading-edge foundry market TSMC serves (Apple, Nvidia, AMD as named customers) still has some demand concentration risk on the customer side that a pure percentage of the capex figure does not capture, but the capex itself is unambiguously reachable through a single, liquid, dual-listed name.

capture_odds.rationale: Leading-edge foundry capacity is the textbook qualification-locked, pricing-power case: TSMC holds roughly 72% of the global foundry market and effectively all commercially available sub-3nm capacity, and its customers (Apple, Nvidia, AMD) cannot single-source an alternative at the same node in the appraisal window. That argues for a score at or above 85. Held down to 75 rather than higher because TSMC's own guidance, carried in the candidate's occurrence record (not independently re-fetched this run, so weighted but not scored as a fresh citation), states the Arizona expansion itself dilutes gross margin by 2-3 points in the near term and 3-4 points longer term because US fabs cost at least 50% more to build and run than Taiwan fabs. That is a real, company-guided erosion of how much of this specific $265B converts to durable incremental profit versus simply defending existing share at a lower margin, so the leg is scored as strong capture with a stated, quantified drag rather than at the ceiling.

timing_fit.rationale: Money is already moving: Arizona fab one has run N4 in volume since late 2024 (per the candidate's own occurrence record) and fab two is under construction, so part of the $265B program is inside the 2-5 year window by construction today. Held at 72 rather than higher because TSMC explicitly declined to commit a build-out schedule for the newly announced fabs: this run's own fetch confirms TSMC stated no construction timeline for the four new fabs, with pace set by market demand, so while the capital commitment is dated (2026-07-16) and real, the specific cadence at which it lands inside versus beyond the 2-5 year window is company-discretionary rather than contractually fixed. CEO C.C. Wei's statement that four more plants would 'probably' be built, joining eight fabs already under construction or planned, is directionally supportive but explicitly non-committal language, which is the reason this leg is not scored in the 85+ 'committed and dated' band.
